moat_against: Routine testing is commoditized; prices are set by payers and CMS/PAMA, not by Labcorp — little pricing power on core volume
Quest Diagnostics matches Labcorp's scale and contests every managed-care contract — no share lock-in
Hospital in-sourcing, regional labs, and direct-to-consumer entrants pressure the low end
Recurring reimbursement, billing-regulation, and cybersecurity risk in healthcare data
Biopharma services revenue rides pharma R&D spending cycles
moat_for: Duopoly scale with Quest: national network of 2,000+ patient service centers and logistics regionals cannot replicate
Payer and health-system contracts / preferred-provider status drive recurring volume; hospital outsourcing trend is a tailwind
Broad and specialty test menu — oncology, neurology, women's health growing double-digit
Biopharma Laboratory Services backlog of $8.7B (Q2 2026) gives contracted revenue visibility
Longitudinal test-result data scale and physician-workflow IT integrations create switching friction
moat_justification: US clinical-lab duopoly scale with Quest — national patient-service-center network, payer and health-system contracts, broad specialty test menu, and an $8.7B Biopharma Laboratory Services backlog give real scale and switching friction; but routine testing is commoditized, pricing is set by payers/CMS rather than Labcorp, and Quest matches its scale on every contract, so pricing power and durability cap the score at moderate-strong.
name: Labcorp Holdings Inc.
one_liner: High-quality duopoly lab franchise, moat 6/10, but priced far above owner's-earnings value — weighted IRR 8.3%, IV@15 $140 vs $319.51 price; doesn't clear 15% until ~$140, and even the super-bull case returns only 12.1%.
